# Sill

> Sill is a native app for software developers on Mac, iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch that writes their daily standup from the work they already do, and keeps receipts on everything they're waiting on from other people.

- What it does: on the Mac, Sill reads local git history (commit messages and times only, never source code) and combines it with the tasks you finish and the follow-ups you log, to write Yesterday / Today / Blockers. One tap copies it for Slack, Teams, Jira or email.
- Receipts: for each blocker (an API, a design, a review, access) Sill shows how long you've waited and how many times you followed up, e.g. "day 6, asked 3x", and includes that in the standup.
- Worklog: a timeline of commits, finished tasks, notes, follow-ups and focus sessions; copy a worklog for any date range.
- Privacy: no account, no server, no analytics. The App Store privacy label is "Data Not Collected". Data stays on device and in the user's private iCloud.
- Platforms: one universal purchase for macOS (window + menu bar), iOS, iPadOS and watchOS. Git commits are read only by the Mac app and never sync; iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch track tasks and blockers.
- Price: free on the App Store, including the set-time standup reminder. Sill Pro is an optional paid upgrade: a self-review generator for periods longer than 7 days (drafted on device with Apple Intelligence where available), a calendar-following reminder, and more than 3 open blockers at a time (free tracks 3).
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6823163147

## Free tools

- [Standup generator from git log](https://dmaulikr.github.io/sill-site/standup-generator.html): paste git log output, add today's plan and blockers, copy a standup formatted for Slack, Microsoft Teams, Jira or plain text. Drops merge commits and conventional-commit prefixes, keeps ticket IDs, groups multi-repo output by repo. Runs in the browser; nothing is uploaded.
